subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finhealth.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@finhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Pain points & constraints (call notes):
- Regulated PHI workload: data residency and strict audit requirements (SOC2 + HITRUST considerations flagged).
- Customer-managed keys required (KMS/HSM) for encryption at rest; FinHealth needs full key control and rotation policies.
- Network: strict egress controls, IP whitelisting, and the requirement for VPC peering or privately routed endpoints (no internet egress for production inference traffic).
- Air-gap / staging requirement: a completely isolated environment for validation before any production connectivity; no outbound telemetry to third-party services unless approved.
- SSO: SAML-based IdP integration and per-team RBAC for admin operations.

Current stack (what we heard):
- Primary cloud: AWS (GovCloud for some workloads), internal KMS/HSM via AWS CloudHSM, Okta SAML for SSO.
- Model inference today: a mix of batch/offline on-prem and some third-party API calls for prototypes.

Success criteria (customer-facing):
- Production deployment in a VPC with no public egress and support for FinHealth-managed KMS/HSM.
- Audit evidence for SOC2 controls and access logs retained per FinHealth policy (7 years).
- SLA target: 99.9% uptime and p99 latency under 200ms for small-text generation workloads (initial target).
- Ability to run a short PoC in an isolated VPC to validate throughput and security controls before contract signature.

Next steps (owners & timing):
1) Redwood to provide: SOC2 questionnaire + high-level network/topology diagram and mutual action plan (MAP) — Marissa (by Thu 3/6). Attachment: FinHealth-SOC2-questions.pdf, MAP stub attached.
2) Technical deep-dive: Dev Patel to join a session to map out VPC peering, HSM integration, and deployment options (schedule 60–90 min) — proposed next week (Mar 9–11).
3) PoC scope: Agree on test dataset, telemetry allowed, and maintenance windows (Samir to confirm budget & timeline).
4) Pricing & procurement: Rachel will draft a dedicated capacity estimate and high-level commercial terms once PoC scope confirmed.

Thanks — we’ll treat the PoC as the gating item before formal procurement.

Best,

On Wed, 4 Mar 2026 at 15:12 Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections or additions.

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Residency: Production data must remain in US GovCloud regions only; any backup/replica must also be kept in-region.
- HSM: We require a FIPS-validated HSM for root key material; CloudHSM or a customer-managed HSM that you can integrate with is acceptable.
- Air-gap: Our security team will expect no outgoing metrics/telemetry from the PoC unless explicitly listed in the MAP and signed off.
- SSO: Yes, Okta SAML. Also need SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle (if available).
- Maintenance: Waived weekend maintenance windows preferred; planned changes require 72-hour notice.

Budget/timebox: We’re targeting a Q2 2026 contract if the PoC validates security and latency. For the PoC, we’d like a 2-week test window with synthetic traffic that simulates 50 TPS for 30-second bursts.

Assigning next actions on our side:
- Elaine will pull together the security signoffs and provide contact for compliance evidence requests.
- I’ll confirm the PoC dataset and share a list of IPs that will need allowlisting.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the SOC2 questionnaire and MAP.

—Samir
